spec.description: Every active fire NASA satellites detected since 2000, as the A5 cells of the Portolan FIRMS mirror read in the browser: a time brush over years or days, a latitude raster where the fire seasons swing across the equator, a calendar of months, countries and a strip of filters that cross-filter one another with Chaski and Mosaic, and a map whose cells give way to the single detections of the window when zoomed in.

options.content:
**NASA FIRMS active fire detections** since November 2000, from the
[Portolan mirror](https://portolan-mirrors.github.io/firms-catalog/) on
[Source Cooperative](https://source.coop/portolan-mirrors/firms-catalog) (CC0-1.0; NASA LANCE FIRMS is the producer and
the authority). This dashboard reads the aggregates the mirror builds beside the 630 million detections: each A5 cell of
resolution 5 with its count per day for the current year (`year=YYYY/aggregate-r5.parquet`) and per month for the whole
record (`alltime-r5.parquet`), the same grid and buckets the
[Portolan FIRMS explorer](https://portolan-mirrors.github.io/firms-catalog/) draws from its PMTiles. Your browser reads
them with Chaski; the server only turns the cell outlines into GeoJSON and gives each cell a country
([Natural Earth](https://www.naturalearthdata.com/) 1:110m, the one covering most of it). Zoomed in, the map shows the detections themselves (`year=YYYY/detections.parquet`), which the server reads only where the view is: the files are sorted along a Hilbert curve, so a few row groups of each year cover it.

- **Counts depend on the fleet.** MODIS on Terra (2000) and Aqua (2002), then VIIRS on Suomi-NPP (2012), NOAA-20 (2018)
  and NOAA-21 (2024): each adds overpasses, and the count of 2012 is 5.5 times that of 2011 with no change in fire.
  The calendar shows shares within each year for that reason.
- **The aggregates hold counts only**, per cell and bucket: no satellite, day or night, or fire radiative power per
  day. The detections layer of the zoomed-in map has them.
- **The all-time file is rebuilt less often** than the year files, so the current year comes from its own file, by
  day and rolled up to months.

**Credits.** The mirror, its A5 aggregates and the explorer that inspired this dashboard are the work of **Chris Holmes** ([Portolan](https://www.portolan-sdi.org)), who tells how he built them in [Building Portolan: FIRMS](https://www.portolan-sdi.org/es/blog/building-portolan-firms).

spec.rawSql:
-- Detections per bucket of the chosen archive (days of this year, or months
-- since 2000) under the other filters: months of the year, latitudes,
-- continent or country, drawn area. In grey behind, every detection on Earth.
-- On the monthly archive, a tick marks each VIIRS satellite joining the fleet:
-- counts jump there with no change in fire.
-- It reads those variables one by one, never the window it writes, so
-- dragging does not ask it again.
WITH area AS (
  SELECT list_transform(xs, lambda x: x - 360 * round(coalesce(list_avg(xs), 0) / 360)) AS xs, ys
  FROM (
    SELECT
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 1) AS xs,
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 0) AS ys
    FROM (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract_all($area, '-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?') AS DOUBLE[]) AS n)
  )
),
inside AS (
  -- The cells whose centre is in the drawn area (all of them with none drawn).
  SELECT a5
  FROM $cells, area
  WHERE len(area.xs) = 0 OR (longitude BETWEEN list_min(area.xs) AND list_max(area.xs)
    AND latitude BETWEEN list_min(area.ys) AND list_max(area.ys)
    AND list_sum(list_transform(range(1, len(area.xs) + 1), lambda i:
      CASE WHEN (area.ys[i] > latitude) <> (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] > latitude)
            AND longitude < (area.xs[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.xs[i]) * (latitude - area.ys[i]) / (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.ys[i]) + area.xs[i]
           THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) % 2 = 1)
)
SELECT f.time,
       coalesce(sum(f.n) FILTER (WHERE i.a5 IS NOT NULL
         AND f.month IN (${months})
         AND f.latitude >= coalesce(try_cast($lat_lo AS DOUBLE), -90)
         AND f.latitude <= coalesce(try_cast($lat_hi AS DOUBLE), 90)
         AND ($continent = '' OR f.continent = $continent)
         AND ($country = '' OR f.country = $country)), 0)::DOUBLE AS "Detections",
       sum(f.n)::DOUBLE AS "Everywhere",
       NULL::DOUBLE AS "A VIIRS satellite joins"
FROM $fire AS f LEFT JOIN inside AS i USING (a5)
GROUP BY f.time
UNION ALL
SELECT t, NULL, NULL, 1
FROM (VALUES (TIMESTAMP '2012-01-20'), (TIMESTAMP '2018-04-01'), (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-17')) AS v(t)
WHERE $archive = 'month'
ORDER BY time

spec.description: Detections in each bucket of the chosen archive, in the picked country or drawn area; in grey behind, every detection on Earth. On the monthly archive the ticks under the track mark the three VIIRS satellites joining (2012, 2018, 2024): each one multiplies the count with no change in fire. Drag across the track to pick a window; the map, the ranking and the figures keep that window. The bar stays pinned at the top once the panel scrolls away.

It follows every other filter. Click a month to keep that month of every year in the other panels (shift-click to add more); click it again to clear. On the archive of this year by day, it is one row.

spec.rawSql:
-- Countries by detections under every filter but the country pick; the
-- fifteen largest, and the picked one even when it is not. latitude/longitude:
-- the middle of its fire, weighted by detections.
WITH agg AS (
  SELECT country, continent, sum(n)::DOUBLE AS detections,
         round(sum(latitude * n) / sum(n), 3) AS latitude,
         round(sum(longitude * n) / sum(n), 3) AS longitude
  FROM $fire
  WHERE $__crossfilter($fireFilters, -country)
  GROUP BY ALL
)
SELECT * FROM (SELECT *, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY detections DESC) AS rank FROM agg)
WHERE rank <= 15 OR country = $country
ORDER BY rank

spec.description: The fifteen countries with the most detections in the window and the drawn area, coloured by continent (orange Africa, green South America, blue North America, red Asia, purple Europe, yellow Oceania). Each A5 cell counts for the country that covers most of it, so border regions and small countries are approximate. Click a bar to keep that country and fly the map to it; click it again to clear.
spec.title: Countries by detections

spec.description: Countries with at least one detection in the window and the drawn area. Each A5 cell counts for the country that covers most of it.

spec.description: Every filter of the dashboard in one strip. Open a pill to brush a range (time, latitude) or pick values (month of the year, continent, country); each control counts what the other filters leave. It counts rows of the archive, one per cell and bucket with a fire, not detections. The map sets the drawn area. × clears a filter, Clear all every one.

Every bucket of the archive placed by its time (across) and the latitude of its A5 cell (up), shaded by its detections as a share of the world's mean bucket in that year, so the satellites that joined the fleet in 2012, 2018 and 2024 do not light up the later years. The dry seasons swing across the equator each year: the Sahel and Central Africa from November to February, southern Africa and the Amazon from June to October, the boreal forest in summer. It follows every other filter. Drag across it to pick a window: the time brush, the map and every panel follow.
spec.title: Fire by latitude, bucket by bucket

options.content:
**How to read it.** This is the long view: the A5 aggregates the Portolan mirror publishes, about 5 MB,
read and joined once in your browser, where every panel filters them. *Archive* switches between this year by day and
every month since 2000. Drag across the time brush or the latitude raster to pick a window, click a month in the
calendar to keep that month of every year, click a country, draw an area on the map, or open a pill of the filter strip.
**Zoom the map in** and the cells give way to the single detections of the window in the view, read on the server.

For satellites, day and night and fire radiative power of the last days, open
[the last eight days, every detection](/d/firms-active-fires).

spec.rawSql:
-- The A5 cells with a detection under every filter but the area drawn on the
-- map itself (so the map keeps its context), with how many. None once the map
-- is zoomed in to a view under 25 degrees across: there the detections of
-- query B take their place (the same test, on the same viewport variables).
SELECT c.country, agg.detections, round(log10(agg.detections), 2) AS log_detections, c.geojson
FROM (
  SELECT a5, sum(n)::DOUBLE AS detections FROM $fire
  WHERE $__crossfilter($fireFilters, -drawn)
    AND NOT coalesce(try_cast($e AS DOUBLE) - try_cast($w AS DOUBLE) <= 25
                     AND try_cast($n AS DOUBLE) - try_cast($s AS DOUBLE) <= 25, false)
  GROUP BY a5
) AS agg
JOIN $cells AS c USING (a5)
ORDER BY agg.detections

spec.description: Zoomed out, each pentagon is an A5 cell of resolution 5 (about 200 km across, the grid the Portolan explorer draws) coloured by its detections under every filter, on a log scale. Zoom in to a view under 25 degrees across and the cells give way to the single detections of the brushed window in the view, read on the server from the yearly files of the mirror (a few seconds; the strongest 100,000 by FRP), coloured by fire radiative power. Draw a polygon or rectangle to keep that area in the other panels; the map itself keeps showing everything.

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: every A5 cell of resolution 5 (about 200 km across) that has
-- had a fire since 2000, with its outline as GeoJSON, its centre, and the
-- country that covers most of it (Natural Earth 1:110m). Cells first burning
-- this year come from the year file, which is rebuilt more often than the
-- all-time one. The A5 id is a 64-bit integer, sent as text so it survives
-- JSON. The two polar caps are left out: no fire there, and their outlines
-- span the globe.
WITH alltime AS (
  SELECT a5_cell, geometry FROM read_parquet('https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/firms-catalog/detections/alltime-r5.parquet')
),
fresh AS (
  SELECT a5_cell, geometry FROM read_parquet('https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/firms-catalog/detections/year=' || year(current_date)::VARCHAR || '/aggregate-r5.parquet')
  WHERE a5_cell NOT IN (SELECT a5_cell FROM alltime)
),
cells AS (
  -- The cells say OGC:CRS84 and Natural Earth EPSG:4326, the same axes here:
  -- the plain GEOMETRY type drops the label so the two can be compared.
  SELECT a5_cell, geometry::GEOMETRY AS geom FROM (SELECT * FROM alltime UNION ALL SELECT * FROM fresh)
  WHERE ST_YMax(geometry) < 89 AND ST_YMin(geometry) > -89
),
countries AS (
  SELECT name, continent, geom::GEOMETRY AS g FROM ST_Read('https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector@v5.1.2/geojson/ne_110m_admin_0_countries.geojson')
),
hits AS (
  SELECT cells.a5_cell, n.name, n.continent, ST_Area(ST_Intersection(n.g, cells.geom)) AS overlap
  FROM cells JOIN countries AS n ON ST_Intersects(n.g, cells.geom)
),
best AS (
  SELECT a5_cell, arg_max(name, overlap) AS country, arg_max(continent, overlap) AS continent
  FROM hits GROUP BY a5_cell
)
SELECT cells.a5_cell::VARCHAR AS a5,
       coalesce(best.country, 'Ocean or unassigned') AS country,
       coalesce(best.continent, 'Ocean') AS continent,
       round(ST_Y(ST_Centroid(cells.geom)), 3) AS latitude,
       round(ST_X(ST_Centroid(cells.geom)), 3) AS longitude,
       ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_ReducePrecision(cells.geom, 0.001))::VARCHAR AS geojson
FROM cells LEFT JOIN best USING (a5_cell)

source.sql:
-- In the browser: the A5 aggregates the Portolan mirror publishes beside the
-- detections, read straight from Source Cooperative (CORS open, about 5 MB):
-- the current year with one column per day (count_YYYYMMDD) and the whole
-- record with one per month (count_YYYYMM). UNPIVOT turns those columns into
-- rows, one per cell and bucket with a fire. level day is this year by day;
-- level month is every month since November 2000, this year rolled up from
-- its days because the all-time file is rebuilt less often. The panels join
-- the cells for country and centre, so this loads beside them, not after.
WITH year_file AS (
  SELECT * EXCLUDE (geometry, bbox) FROM read_parquet('https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/firms-catalog/detections/year=' || year(current_date)::VARCHAR || '/aggregate-r5.parquet')
),
days AS (
  SELECT a5_cell::VARCHAR AS a5, strptime(substr(bucket, 7), '%Y%m%d') AS time, n::DOUBLE AS n
  FROM year_file UNPIVOT (n FOR bucket IN (COLUMNS('^count_20')))
  WHERE n > 0
),
months AS (
  SELECT a5_cell::VARCHAR AS a5, strptime(substr(bucket, 7) || '01', '%Y%m%d') AS time, n::DOUBLE AS n
  FROM (SELECT * EXCLUDE (geometry, bbox) FROM read_parquet('https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/firms-catalog/detections/alltime-r5.parquet'))
    UNPIVOT (n FOR bucket IN (COLUMNS('^count_[0-9]{6}$')))
  WHERE n > 0 AND bucket < 'count_' || year(current_date)::VARCHAR
),
buckets AS (
  SELECT 'day' AS level, time, n, a5 FROM days
  UNION ALL SELECT 'month', time, n, a5 FROM months
  UNION ALL SELECT 'month', date_trunc('month', time), sum(n), a5 FROM days GROUP BY date_trunc('month', time), a5
)
SELECT level, time, n, a5 FROM buckets
-- Sorted by level and time, so a panel reading one window skips the rest.
ORDER BY level, time

-- In the browser, once per archive: every bucket of the chosen archive (a day
-- of this year, or a month since 2000) of every A5 cell with a fire, joined
-- once to its cell for the country, the continent and the centre, with the
-- year and the month it falls in. w is its detections as a percentage of the
-- world's mean bucket in that year: the satellites that joined the fleet
-- (2012, 2018, 2024) multiplied the counts with no change in fire, and w takes
-- that out, so the calendar and the latitude raster compare years. One table
-- that the Mosaic panels, the filters and every SQL panel below read, sorted
-- by time so a window reads only its row groups.
WITH b AS (
  SELECT time, n, a5 FROM $counts WHERE level = $archive
),
yearly AS (
  SELECT year(time) AS year, sum(n) / count(DISTINCT time) AS mean_bucket FROM b GROUP BY ALL
)
SELECT b.time, b.n, b.a5, c.country, c.continent, c.latitude, c.longitude,
       year(b.time)::INTEGER AS year, strftime(b.time, '%b') AS month,
       (100 * b.n / yearly.mean_bucket)::DOUBLE AS w
FROM b
JOIN $cells AS c USING (a5)
JOIN yearly ON yearly.year = year(b.time)
ORDER BY b.time
